units.rightText: Then shall ye remember your evil ways, and your doings that were not good; and ye shall loathe yourselves in your own sight for your iniquities and for your abominations.

units.leftText: It is not for your sake that I will act, declares the Lord GOD — let it be known to you. Be ashamed and disgraced for your ways, O house of Israel!
units.rightText: Nor for your sake do I this, saith the Lord Jehovah, be it known unto you: be ashamed and confounded for your ways, O house of Israel.

units.leftText: This is what the Lord GOD says: On the day I cleanse you from all your iniquities, I will cause the cities to be resettled and the ruins to be rebuilt.
units.rightText: Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: In the day that I cleanse you from all your iniquities, I will cause the cities to be inhabited, and the waste places shall be builded.

units.leftText: The desolate land will be cultivated instead of lying desolate in the sight of all who pass through.
units.rightText: And the land that was desolate shall be tilled, whereas it was a desolation in the sight of all that passed by.

units.leftText: Then they will say, ‘This land that was desolate has become like the garden of Eden. The cities that were once ruined, desolate, and destroyed are now fortified and inhabited.’
units.rightText: And they shall say, This land that was desolate is become like the garden of Eden; and the waste and desolate and ruined cities are fortified and inhabited.

units.leftText: Then the nations around you that remain will know that I, the LORD, have rebuilt what was destroyed, and I have replanted what was desolate. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it.
units.rightText: Then the nations that are left round about you shall know that I, Jehovah, have builded the ruined places, and planted that which was desolate: I, Jehovah, have spoken it, and I will do it.

units.leftText: This is what the Lord GOD says: Once again I will hear the plea of the house of Israel and do for them this: I will multiply their people like a flock.
units.rightText: Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: For this, moreover, will I be inquired of by the house of Israel, to do it for them: I will increase them with men like a flock.

units.leftText: Like the numerous flocks for sacrifices at Jerusalem during her appointed feasts, so the ruined cities will be filled with flocks of people. Then they will know that I am the LORD.”
units.rightText: As the flock for sacrifice, as the flock of Jerusalem in her appointed feasts, so shall the waste cities be filled with flocks of men; and they shall know that I am Jehovah.

units.leftText: The hand of the LORD was upon me, and He brought me out by His Spirit and set me down in the middle of the valley, and it was full of bones.
units.rightText: The hand of Jehovah was upon me, and he brought me out in the Spirit of Jehovah, and set me down in the midst of the valley; and it was full of bones.

units.leftText: He led me all around among them, and I saw a great many bones on the floor of the valley, and indeed, they were very dry.
units.rightText: And he caused me to pass by them round about: and, behold, there were very many in the open valley; and, lo, they were very dry.

units.leftText: Then He asked me, “Son of man, can these bones come to life?” “O Lord GOD,” I replied, “only You know.”
units.rightText: And he said unto me, Son of man, can these bones live? And I answered, O Lord Jehovah, thou knowest.

units.leftText: And He said to me, “Prophesy concerning these bones and tell them, ‘Dry bones, hear the word of the LORD!
units.rightText: Again he said unto me, Prophesy over these bones, and say unto them, O ye dry bones, hear the word of Jehovah.

units.leftText: This is what the Lord GOD says to these bones: I will cause breath to enter you, and you will come to life.
units.rightText: Thus saith the Lord Jehovah unto these bones: Behold, I will cause breath to enter into you, and ye shall live.
leftNotes: 37:5 Or spirit; also in verses 6, 9, and 10

units.leftText: I will attach tendons to you and make flesh grow upon you and cover you with skin. I will put breath within you so that you will come to life. Then you will know that I am the LORD.’”
units.rightText: And I will lay sinews upon you, and will bring up flesh upon you, and cover you with skin, and put breath in you, and ye shall live; and ye shall know that I am Jehovah.

units.leftText: So I prophesied as I had been commanded. And as I prophesied, there was suddenly a noise, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to bone.
units.rightText: So I prophesied as I was commanded: and as I prophesied, there was a noise, and, behold, an earthquake; and the bones came together, bone to its bone.

units.leftText: As I looked on, tendons appeared on them, flesh grew, and skin covered them; but there was no breath in them.
units.rightText: And I beheld, and, lo, there were sinews upon them, and flesh came up, and skin covered them above; but there was no breath in them.

units.leftText: Then He said to me, “Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, son of man, and tell the breath that this is what the Lord GOD says: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe into these slain, so that they may live!”
units.rightText: Then said he unto me, Prophesy unto the wind, prophesy, son of man, and say to the wind, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live.

units.leftText: So I prophesied as He had commanded me, and the breath entered them, and they came to life and stood on their feet — a vast army.
units.rightText: So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.

units.leftText: Then He said to me, “Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel. Look, they are saying, ‘Our bones are dried up, and our hope has perished; we are cut off.’
units.rightText: Then he said unto me, Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel: behold, they say, Our bones are dried up, and our hope is lost; we are clean cut off.

units.leftText: Therefore prophesy and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘O My people, I will open your graves and bring you up from them, and I will bring you back to the land of Israel.
units.rightText: Therefore prophesy, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Behold, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves, O my people; and I will bring you into the land of Israel.

units.leftText: Then you, My people, will know that I am the LORD, when I open your graves and bring you up from them.
units.rightText: And ye shall know that I am Jehovah, when I have opened your graves, and caused you to come up out of your graves, O my people.

units.leftText: I will put My Spirit in you and you will live, and I will settle you in your own land. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it, declares the LORD.’” One Nation with One King
units.rightText: And I will put my Spirit in you, and ye shall live, and I will place you in your own land: and ye shall know that I, Jehovah, have spoken it and performed it, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
units.rightText: The word of Jehovah came again unto me, saying,

units.leftText: “And you, son of man, take a single stick and write on it: ‘Belonging to Judah and to the Israelites associated with him.’ Then take another stick and write on it: ‘Belonging to Joseph— the stick of Ephraim— and to all the house of Israel associated with him.’
units.rightText: And thou, son of man, take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions: then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions:
leftNotes: 37:16 Or branch; also in verses 17, 19, and 20

units.leftText: Then join them together into one stick, so that they become one in your hand.
units.rightText: and join them for thee one to another into one stick, that they may become one in thy hand.

units.leftText: When your people ask you, ‘Won’t you explain to us what you mean by these?’
units.rightText: And when the children of thy people shall speak unto thee, saying, Wilt thou not show us what thou meanest by these?

units.leftText: you are to tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel associated with him, and I will put them together with the stick of Judah. I will make them into a single stick, and they will become one in My hand.’
units.rightText: say unto them, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Behold, I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel his companions; and I will put them with it, even with the stick of Judah, and make them one stick, and they shall be one in my hand.

units.leftText: When the sticks on which you write are in your hand and in full view of the people,
units.rightText: And the sticks whereon thou writest shall be in thy hand before their eyes.

units.leftText: you are to tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will take the Israelites out of the nations to which they have gone, and I will gather them from all around and bring them into their own land.
units.rightText: And say unto them, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the nations, whither they are gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:

units.leftText: I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, and one king will rule over all of them. Then they will no longer be two nations and will never again be divided into two kingdoms.
units.rightText: and I will make them one nation in the land, upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all; and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all;

units.leftText: They will no longer defile themselves with their idols or detestable images, or with any of their transgressions. I will save them from all their apostasies by which they sinned, and I will cleanse them. Then they will be My people, and I will be their God.
units.rightText: neither shall they defile themselves any more with their idols, nor with their detestable things, nor with any of their transgressions; but I will save them out of all their dwelling-places, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.
leftNotes: 37:23 Many Hebrew manuscripts (see also LXX); most Hebrew manuscripts all their dwelling places where they sinned

units.leftText: My servant David will be king over them, and there will be one shepherd for all of them. They will follow My ordinances and keep and observe My statutes.
units.rightText: And my servant David shall be king over them; and they all shall have one shepherd: they shall also walk in mine ordinances, and observe my statutes, and do them.

units.leftText: They will live in the land that I gave to My servant Jacob, where your fathers lived. They will live there forever with their children and grandchildren, and My servant David will be their prince forever.
units.rightText: And they shall dwell in the land that I have given unto Jacob my servant, wherein your fathers dwelt; and they shall dwell therein, they, and their children, and their children’s children, for ever: and David my servant shall be their prince for ever.

units.leftText: And I will make a covenant of peace with them; it will be an everlasting covenant. I will establish them and multiply them, and I will set My sanctuary among them forever.
units.rightText: Moreover I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them; and I will place them, and multiply them, and will set my sanctuary in the midst of them for evermore.

units.leftText: My dwelling place will be with them; I will be their God, and they will be My people.
units.rightText: My tabernacle also shall be with them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
leftNotes: 37:27 Or My tabernacle
37:27 Cited in 2 Corinthians 6:16|2CO 6:16*

units.leftText: Then the nations will know that I the LORD sanctify Israel, when My sanctuary is among them forever.’”
units.rightText: And the nations shall know that I am Jehovah that sanctifieth Israel, when my sanctuary shall be in the midst of them for evermore.

units.leftText: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
units.rightText: And the word of Jehovah came unto me, saying,

units.leftText: “Son of man, set your face against Gog of the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. Prophesy against him
units.rightText: Son of man, set thy face toward Gog, of the land of Magog, the prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal, and prophesy against him,
leftNotes: 38:2 Or of Magog, the prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal

units.leftText: and declare that this is what the Lord GOD says: Behold, I am against you, O Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
units.rightText: and say, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Behold, I am against thee, O Gog, prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal:
leftNotes: 38:3 Or Gog, the prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal

units.leftText: I will turn you around, put hooks in your jaws, and bring you out with all your army — your horses, your horsemen in full armor, and a great company armed with shields and bucklers, all brandishing their swords.
units.rightText: and I will turn thee about, and put hooks into thy jaws, and I will bring thee forth, and all thine army, horses and horsemen, all of them clothed in full armor, a great company with buckler and shield, all of them handling swords:

units.leftText: Persia, Cush, and Put will accompany them, all with shields and helmets,
units.rightText: Persia, Cush, and Put with them, all of them with shield and helmet;
leftNotes: 38:5 That is, the upper Nile region

units.leftText: as well as Gomer with all its troops, and Beth-togarmah from the far north with all its troops— the many nations with you.
units.rightText: Gomer, and all his hordes; the house of Togarmah in the uttermost parts of the north, and all his hordes; even many peoples with thee.

units.leftText: Get ready; prepare yourself, you and all your company gathered around you; you will be their guard.
units.rightText: Be thou prepared, yea, prepare thyself, thou, and all thy companies that are assembled unto thee, and be thou a guard unto them.

units.leftText: After a long time you will be summoned. In the latter years you will enter a land that has recovered from war, whose people were gathered from many nations to the mountains of Israel, which had long been desolate. They had been brought out from the nations, and all now dwell securely.
units.rightText: After many days thou shalt be visited: in the latter years thou shalt come into the land that is brought back from the sword, that is gathered out of many peoples, upon the mountains of Israel, which have been a continual waste; but it is brought forth out of the peoples, and they shall dwell securely, all of them.

units.leftText: You and all your troops, and many peoples with you will go up, advancing like a thunderstorm; you will be like a cloud covering the land.
units.rightText: And thou shalt ascend, thou shalt come like a storm, thou shalt be like a cloud to cover the land, thou, and all thy hordes, and many peoples with thee.

units.leftText: This is what the Lord GOD says: On that day, thoughts will arise in your mind, and you will devise an evil plan.
units.rightText: Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: It shall come to pass in that day, that things shall come into thy mind, and thou shalt devise an evil device:

units.leftText: You will say, ‘I will go up against a land of unwalled villages; I will come against a quiet people who dwell securely, all of them living without walls or bars or gates—
units.rightText: and thou shalt say, I will go up to the land of unwalled villages; I will go to them that are at rest, that dwell securely, all of them dwelling without walls, and having neither bars nor gates;

units.leftText: in order to seize the spoil and carry off the plunder, to turn a hand against the desolate places now inhabited and against a people gathered from the nations, who have acquired livestock and possessions and who live at the center of the land.’
units.rightText: to take the spoil and to take the prey; to turn thy hand against the waste places that are now inhabited, and against the people that are gathered out of the nations, that have gotten cattle and goods, that dwell in the middle of the earth.

units.leftText: Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish with all its villages will ask, ‘Have you come to capture the plunder? Have you assembled your hordes to carry away loot, to make off with silver and gold, to take cattle and goods, to seize great spoil?’
units.rightText: Sheba, and Dedan, and the merchants of Tarshish, with all the young lions thereof, shall say unto thee, Art thou come to take the spoil? hast thou assembled thy company to take the prey? to carry away silver and gold, to take away cattle and goods, to take great spoil?
leftNotes: 38:13 Or young lions

units.leftText: Therefore prophesy, son of man, and tell Gog that this is what the Lord GOD says: On that day when My people Israel are dwelling securely, will you not take notice of this?
units.rightText: Therefore, son of man, prophesy, and say unto Gog, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: In that day when my people Israel dwelleth securely, shalt thou not know it?
leftNotes: 38:14 LXX will you not rouse yourself?

units.leftText: And you will come from your place out of the far north— you and many peoples with you, all riding horses— a mighty horde, a huge army.
units.rightText: And thou shalt come from thy place out of the uttermost parts of the north, thou, and many peoples with thee, all of them riding upon horses, a great company and a mighty army;

units.leftText: You will advance against My people Israel like a cloud covering the land. It will happen in the latter days, O Gog, that I will bring you against My land, so that the nations may know Me when I show Myself holy in you before their eyes.
units.rightText: and thou shalt come up against my people Israel, as a cloud to cover the land: it shall come to pass in the latter days, that I will bring thee against my land, that the nations may know me, when I shall be sanctified in thee, O Gog, before their eyes.

units.leftText: This is what the Lord GOD says: Are you the one of whom I have spoken in former days through My servants, the prophets of Israel, who in those times prophesied for years that I would bring you against them?
units.rightText: Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Art thou he of whom I spake in old time by my servants the prophets of Israel, that prophesied in those days for many years that I would bring thee against them?

units.leftText: Now on that day when Gog comes against the land of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, My wrath will flare up.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, when Gog shall come against the land of Israel, saith the Lord Jehovah, that my wrath shall come up into my nostrils.

units.leftText: In My zeal and fiery rage I proclaim that on that day there will be a great earthquake in the land of Israel.
units.rightText: For in my jealousy and in the fire of my wrath have I spoken, Surely in that day there shall be a great shaking in the land of Israel;

units.leftText: The fish of the sea, the birds of the air, the beasts of the field, every creature that crawls upon the ground, and all mankind on the face of the earth will tremble at My presence. The mountains will be thrown down, the cliffs will collapse, and every wall will fall to the ground.
units.rightText: so that the fishes of the sea, and the birds of the heavens, and the beasts of the field, and all creeping things that creep upon the earth, and all the men that are upon the face of the earth, shall shake at my presence, and the mountains shall be thrown down, and the steep places shall fall, and every wall shall fall to the ground.

units.leftText: And I will summon a sword against Gog on all My mountains, declares the Lord GOD, and every man’s sword will be against his brother.
units.rightText: And I will call for a sword against him unto all my mountains, saith the Lord Jehovah: every man’s sword shall be against his brother.

units.leftText: I will execute judgment upon him with plague and bloodshed. I will pour out torrents of rain, hailstones, fire, and sulfur on him and on his troops and on the many nations with him.
units.rightText: And with pestilence and with blood will I enter into judgment with him; and I will rain upon him, and upon his hordes, and upon the many peoples that are with him, an overflowing shower, and great hailstones, fire, and brimstone.

units.leftText: I will magnify and sanctify Myself, and I will reveal Myself in the sight of many nations. Then they will know that I am the LORD.[’’]
units.rightText: And I will magnify myself, and sanctify myself, and I will make myself known in the eyes of many nations; and they shall know that I am Jehovah.

units.leftText: “As for you, O son of man, prophesy against Gog and declare that this is what the Lord GOD says: Behold, I am against you, O Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
units.rightText: And thou, son of man, prophesy against Gog, and say, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Behold, I am against thee, O Gog, prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal:
leftNotes: 39:1 Or Gog, prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal

units.leftText: I will turn you around, drive you along, bring you up from the far north, and send you against the mountains of Israel.
units.rightText: and I will turn thee about, and will lead thee on, and will cause thee to come up from the uttermost parts of the north; and I will bring thee upon the mountains of Israel;

units.leftText: Then I will strike the bow from your left hand and dash down the arrows from your right hand.
units.rightText: and I will smite thy bow out of thy left hand, and will cause thine arrows to fall out of thy right hand.

units.leftText: On the mountains of Israel you will fall — you and all your troops and the nations with you. I will give you as food to every kind of ravenous bird and wild beast.
units.rightText: Thou shalt fall upon the mountains of Israel, thou, and all thy hordes, and the peoples that are with thee: I will give thee unto the ravenous birds of every sort, and to the beasts of the field to be devoured.

units.leftText: You will fall in the open field, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.
units.rightText: Thou shalt fall upon the open field; for I have spoken it, saith the Lord Jehovah.

units.leftText: I will send fire on Magog and on those who dwell securely in the coastlands, and they will know that I am the LORD.
units.rightText: And I will send a fire on Magog, and on them that dwell securely in the isles; and they shall know that I am Jehovah.

units.leftText: So I will make My holy name known among My people Israel and will no longer allow it to be profaned. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, the Holy One in Israel.
units.rightText: And my holy name will I make known in the midst of my people Israel; neither will I suffer my holy name to be profaned any more: and the nations shall know that I am Jehovah, the Holy One in Israel.

units.leftText: Yes, it is coming, and it will surely happen, declares the Lord GOD. This is the day of which I have spoken.
units.rightText: Behold, it cometh, and it shall be done, saith the Lord Jehovah; this is the day whereof I have spoken.

units.leftText: Then those who dwell in the cities of Israel will go out, kindle fires, and burn up the weapons— the bucklers and shields, the bows and arrows, the clubs and spears. For seven years they will use them for fuel.
units.rightText: And they that dwell in the cities of Israel shall go forth, and shall make fires of the weapons and burn them, both the shields and the bucklers, the bows and the arrows, and the handstaves, and the spears, and they shall make fires of them seven years;

units.leftText: They will not gather wood from the countryside or cut it from the forests, for they will use the weapons for fuel. They will loot those who looted them and plunder those who plundered them, declares the Lord GOD.
units.rightText: so that they shall take no wood out of the field, neither cut down any out of the forests; for they shall make fires of the weapons; and they shall plunder those that plundered them, and rob those that robbed them, saith the Lord Jehovah.

units.leftText: And on that day I will give Gog a burial place in Israel, the Valley of the Travelers, east of the Sea. It will block those who travel through, because Gog and all his hordes will be buried there. So it will be called the Valley of Hamon-gog.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will give unto Gog a place for burial in Israel, the valley of them that pass through on the east of the sea; and it shall stop them that pass through: and there shall they bury Gog and all his multitude; and they shall call it The valley of Hamon-gog.
leftNotes: 39:11 That is, the Dead Sea
39:11 Hamon-gog means multitude of Gog.

units.leftText: For seven months the house of Israel will be burying them in order to cleanse the land.
units.rightText: And seven months shall the house of Israel be burying them, that they may cleanse the land.

units.leftText: All the people of the land will bury them, and it will bring them renown on the day I display My glory, declares the Lord GOD.
units.rightText: Yea, all the people of the land shall bury them; and it shall be to them a renown in the day that I shall be glorified, saith the Lord Jehovah.
leftNotes: 39:13 Or and the day I display My glory will be a day of renown

units.leftText: And men will be employed to continually pass through the land to cleanse it by burying the invaders who remain on the ground. At the end of the seven months they will begin their search.
units.rightText: And they shall set apart men of continual employment, that shall pass through the land, and, with them that pass through, those that bury them that remain upon the face of the land, to cleanse it: after the end of seven months shall they search.

units.leftText: As they pass through the land, anyone who sees a human bone will set up a pillar next to it, until the gravediggers have buried it in the Valley of Hamon-gog.
units.rightText: And they that pass through the land shall pass through; and when any seeth a man’s bone, then shall he set up a sign by it, till the buriers have buried it in the valley of Hamon-gog.

units.leftText: (Even the city will be named Hamonah. ) And so they will cleanse the land.
units.rightText: And Hamonah shall also be the name of a city. Thus shall they cleanse the land.
leftNotes: 39:16 Hamonah means multitude or horde.

units.leftText: And as for you, son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says: Call out to every kind of bird and to every beast of the field: ‘Assemble and come together from all around to the sacrificial feast that I am preparing for you, a great feast on the mountains of Israel. There you will eat flesh and drink blood.
units.rightText: And thou, son of man, thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Speak unto the birds of every sort, and to every beast of the field, Assemble yourselves, and come; gather yourselves on every side to my sacrifice that I do sacrifice for you, even a great sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel, that ye may eat flesh and drink blood.

units.leftText: You will eat the flesh of the mighty and drink the blood of the princes of the earth as though they were rams, lambs, goats, and bulls — all the fattened animals of Bashan.
units.rightText: Ye shall eat the flesh of the mighty, and drink the blood of the princes of the earth, of rams, of lambs, and of goats, of bullocks, all of them fatlings of Bashan.

units.leftText: At the sacrifice I am preparing, you will eat fat until you are gorged and drink blood until you are drunk.
units.rightText: And ye shall eat fat till ye be full, and drink blood till ye be drunken, of my sacrifice which I have sacrificed for you.

units.leftText: And at My table you will eat your fill of horses and riders, of mighty men and warriors of every kind,’ declares the Lord GOD. Israel to Be Restored
units.rightText: And ye shall be filled at my table with horses and chariots, with mighty men, and with all men of war, saith the Lord Jehovah.

units.leftText: I will display My glory among the nations, and all the nations will see the judgment that I execute and the hand that I lay upon them.
units.rightText: And I will set my glory among the nations; and all the nations shall see my judgment that I have executed, and my hand that I have laid upon them.

units.leftText: From that day forward the house of Israel will know that I am the LORD their God.
units.rightText: So the house of Israel shall know that I am Jehovah their God, from that day and forward.

units.leftText: And the nations will know that the house of Israel went into exile for their iniquity, because they were unfaithful to Me. So I hid My face from them and delivered them into the hands of their enemies, so that they all fell by the sword.
units.rightText: And the nations shall know that the house of Israel went into captivity for their iniquity; because they trespassed against me, and I hid my face from them: so I gave them into the hand of their adversaries, and they fell all of them by the sword.

units.leftText: I dealt with them according to their uncleanness and transgressions, and I hid My face from them.
units.rightText: According to their uncleanness and according to their transgressions did I unto them; and I hid my face from them.

units.leftText: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Now I will restore Jacob from captivity and will have compassion on the whole house of Israel, and I will be jealous for My holy name.
units.rightText: Therefore thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Now will I bring back the captivity of Jacob, and have mercy upon the whole house of Israel; and I will be jealous for my holy name.
leftNotes: 39:25 Or restore the fortunes of Jacob

units.leftText: They will forget their disgrace and all the treachery they committed against Me, when they dwell securely in their land, with no one to frighten them.
units.rightText: And they shall bear their shame, and all their trespasses whereby they have trespassed against me, when they shall dwell securely in their land, and none shall make them afraid;
leftNotes: 39:26 A few Hebrew manuscripts; MT They will bear

units.leftText: When I bring them back from the peoples and gather them out of the lands of their enemies, I will show My holiness in them in the sight of many nations.
units.rightText: when I have brought them back from the peoples, and gathered them out of their enemies’ lands, and am sanctified in them in the sight of many nations.

units.leftText: Then they will know that I am the LORD their God, when I regather them to their own land, not leaving any of them behind after their exile among the nations.
units.rightText: And they shall know that I am Jehovah their God, in that I caused them to go into captivity among the nations, and have gathered them unto their own land; and I will leave none of them any more there;

units.leftText: And I will no longer hide My face from them, for I will pour out My Spirit on the house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.”
units.rightText: neither will I hide my face any more from them; for I have poured out my Spirit upon the house of Israel, saith the Lord Jehovah.

units.leftText: In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month — in the fourteenth year after Jerusalem had been struck down — on that very day the hand of the LORD was upon me, and He took me there.
units.rightText: In the five and twentieth year of our captivity, in the beginning of the year, in the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after that the city was smitten, in the selfsame day, the hand of Jehovah was upon me, and he brought me thither.

units.leftText: In visions of God He took me to the land of Israel and set me on a very high mountain, on whose southern slope was a structure that resembled a city.
units.rightText: In the visions of God brought he me into the land of Israel, and set me down upon a very high mountain, whereon was as it were the frame of a city on the south.

units.leftText: So He took me there, and I saw a man whose appearance was like bronze. He was standing in the gateway with a linen cord and a measuring rod in his hand.
units.rightText: And he brought me thither; and, behold, there was a man, whose appearance was like the appearance of brass, with a line of flax in his hand, and a measuring reed; and he stood in the gate.

units.leftText: “Son of man,” he said to me, “look with your eyes, hear with your ears, and pay attention to everything I am going to show you, for that is why you have been brought here. Report to the house of Israel everything you see.” The East Gate
units.rightText: And the man said unto me, Son of man, behold with thine eyes, and hear with thine ears, and set thy heart upon all that I shall show thee; for, to the intent that I may show them unto thee, art thou brought hither: declare all that thou seest to the house of Israel.

units.leftText: And I saw a wall surrounding the temple area. Now the length of the measuring rod in the man’s hand was six long cubits (each measuring a cubit and a handbreadth), and he measured the wall to be one rod thick and one rod high.
units.rightText: And, behold, a wall on the outside of the house round about, and in the man’s hand a measuring reed six cubits long, of a cubit and a handbreadth each: so he measured the thickness of the building, one reed; and the height, one reed.
leftNotes: 40:5 6 long cubits, the length of the reed used for measuring, is approximately 10.5 feet or 3.2 meters; similarly in verses 6, 7, and 12. The long cubit of about 21 inches or 53.3 centimeters is the basic unit of length throughout Ezekiel 40 to 48.

units.leftText: Then he came to the gate facing east and climbed its steps. He measured the threshold of the gate to be one rod deep.
units.rightText: Then came he unto the gate which looketh toward the east, and went up the steps thereof: and he measured the threshold of the gate, one reed broad; and the other threshold, one reed broad.
leftNotes: 40:6 Hebrew one reed deep, even one threshold, one reed deep.

units.leftText: Each gate chamber was one rod long and one rod wide, and there were five cubits between the gate chambers. The inner threshold of the gate by the portico facing inward was one rod deep.
units.rightText: And every lodge was one reed long, and one reed broad; and the space between the lodges was five cubits; and the threshold of the gate by the porch of the gate toward the house was one reed.
leftNotes: 40:7 5 (long) cubits is approximately 8.75 feet or 2.7 meters; also in verses 30 and 48.

units.leftText: Then he measured the portico of the gateway inside;
units.rightText: He measured also the porch of the gate toward the house, one reed.
leftNotes: 40:8 Literally the portico of the gateway inside, one rod

units.leftText: it was eight cubits deep, and its jambs were two cubits thick. And the portico of the gateway faced the temple.
units.rightText: Then measured he the porch of the gate, eight cubits; and the posts thereof, two cubits; and the porch of the gate was toward the house.
leftNotes: 40:9 8 (long) cubits is approximately 14 feet or 4.3 meters.
40:9 2 (long) cubits is approximately 3.5 feet or 1.1 meters.

units.leftText: There were three gate chambers on each side of the east gate, each with the same measurements, and the gateposts on either side also had the same measurements.
units.rightText: And the lodges of the gate eastward were three on this side, and three on that side; they three were of one measure: and the posts had one measure on this side and on that side.

units.leftText: And he measured the width of the gateway entrance to be ten cubits, and its length was thirteen cubits.
units.rightText: And he measured the breadth of the opening of the gate, ten cubits; and the length of the gate, thirteen cubits;
leftNotes: 40:11 10 (long) cubits is approximately 17.5 feet or 5.3 meters.
40:11 13 (long) cubits is approximately 22.75 feet or 6.9 meters.

units.leftText: In front of each gate chamber was a wall one cubit high, and the gate chambers were six cubits square.
units.rightText: and a border before the lodges, one cubit on this side, and a border, one cubit on that side; and the lodges, six cubits on this side, and six cubits on that side.

units.leftText: Then he measured the gateway from the roof of one gate chamber to the roof of the opposite one; the distance was twenty-five cubits from doorway to doorway.
units.rightText: And he measured the gate from the roof of the one lodge to the roof of the other, a breadth of five and twenty cubits; door against door.
leftNotes: 40:13 25 (long) cubits is approximately 43.75 feet or 13.3 meters; also in verses 21, 25, 29, 30, 33, and 36.

units.leftText: Next he measured the gateposts to be sixty cubits high. The gateway extended around to the gatepost of the courtyard.
units.rightText: He made also posts, threescore cubits; and the court reached unto the posts, round about the gate.
leftNotes: 40:14 60 (long) cubits is approximately 105 feet or 32 meters.

units.leftText: And the distance from the entrance of the gateway to the far end of its inner portico was fifty cubits.
units.rightText: And from the forefront of the gate at the entrance unto the forefront of the inner porch of the gate were fifty cubits.
leftNotes: 40:15 50 (long) cubits is approximately 87.5 feet or 26.7 meters; also in verses 21, 25, 29, 33, and 36.

units.leftText: The gate chambers and their side pillars had beveled windows all around the inside of the gateway. The porticos also had windows all around on the inside. Each side pillar was decorated with palm trees. The Outer Court
units.rightText: And there were closed windows to the lodges, and to their posts within the gate round about, and likewise to the arches; and windows were round about inward; and upon each post were palm-trees.
leftNotes: 40:16 Or gateposts or jambs or projecting walls; here and throughout Ezekiel 40 and 41.

units.leftText: Then he brought me into the outer court, and there were chambers and a pavement laid out all around the court. Thirty chambers faced the pavement,
units.rightText: Then brought he me into the outer court; and, lo, there were chambers and a pavement, made for the court round about: thirty chambers were upon the pavement.

units.leftText: which flanked the gateways and corresponded to the length of the gates; this was the lower pavement.
units.rightText: And the pavement was by the side of the gates, answerable unto the length of the gates, even the lower pavement.

units.leftText: Then he measured the distance from the front of the lower gateway to the outside of the inner court; it was a hundred cubits on the east side as well as on the north. The North Gate
units.rightText: Then he measured the breadth from the forefront of the lower gate unto the forefront of the inner court without, a hundred cubits, both on the east and on the north.
leftNotes: 40:19 100 (long) cubits is approximately 175 feet or 53.3 meters; also in verses 23, 27, and 47.

units.leftText: He also measured the length and width of the gateway of the outer court facing north.
units.rightText: And the gate of the outer court whose prospect is toward the north, he measured the length thereof and the breadth thereof.

units.leftText: Its three gate chambers on each side, its side pillars, and its portico all had the same measurements as the first gate: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
units.rightText: And the lodges thereof were three on this side and three on that side; and the posts thereof and the arches thereof were after the measure of the first gate: the length thereof was fifty cubits, and the breadth five and twenty cubits.

units.leftText: Its windows, portico, and palm trees had the same measurements as those of the gate facing east. Seven steps led up to it, with its portico opposite them.
units.rightText: And the windows thereof, and the arches thereof, and the palm-trees thereof, were after the measure of the gate whose prospect is toward the east; and they went up unto it by seven steps; and the arches thereof were before them.

units.leftText: There was a gate to the inner court facing the north gate, just as there was on the east. He measured the distance from gateway to gateway to be a hundred cubits. The South Gate
units.rightText: And there was a gate to the inner court over against the other gate, both on the north and on the east; and he measured from gate to gate a hundred cubits.

units.leftText: Then he led me to the south side, and I saw a gateway facing south. He measured its side pillars and portico, and they had the same measurements as the others.
units.rightText: And he led me toward the south; and, behold, a gate toward the south: and he measured the posts thereof and the arches thereof according to these measures.

units.leftText: Both the gateway and its portico had windows all around, like the other windows. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
units.rightText: And there were windows in it and in the arches thereof round about, like those windows: the length was fifty cubits, and the breadth five and twenty cubits.

units.leftText: Seven steps led up to it, and its portico was opposite them; it had palm trees on its side pillars, one on each side.
units.rightText: And there were seven steps to go up to it, and the arches thereof were before them; and it had palm-trees, one on this side, and another on that side, upon the posts thereof.

units.leftText: The inner court also had a gate facing south, and he measured the distance from gateway to gateway toward the south to be a hundred cubits. The Gates of the Inner Court
units.rightText: And there was a gate to the inner court toward the south: and he measured from gate to gate toward the south a hundred cubits.

units.leftText: Next he brought me into the inner court through the south gate, and he measured the south gate; it had the same measurements as the others.
units.rightText: Then he brought me to the inner court by the south gate: and he measured the south gate according to these measures;

units.leftText: Its gate chambers, side pillars, and portico had the same measurements as the others. Both the gateway and its portico had windows all around; it was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
units.rightText: and the lodges thereof, and the posts thereof, and the arches thereof, according to these measures: and there were windows in it and in the arches thereof round about; it was fifty cubits long, and five and twenty cubits broad.

units.leftText: (The porticoes around the inner court were twenty-five cubits long and five cubits deep. )
units.rightText: And there were arches round about, five and twenty cubits long, and five cubits broad.
leftNotes: 40:30 The porticoes were approximately 43.75 feet long and 8.75 feet deep (13.3 meters long and 2.7 meters deep).

units.leftText: Its portico faced the outer court, and its side pillars were decorated with palm trees. Eight steps led up to it.
units.rightText: And the arches thereof were toward the outer court; and palm-trees were upon the posts thereof: and the ascent to it had eight steps.

units.leftText: And he brought me to the inner court on the east side, and he measured the gateway; it had the same measurements as the others.
units.rightText: And he brought me into the inner court toward the east: and he measured the gate according to these measures;

units.leftText: Its gate chambers, side pillars, and portico had the same measurements as the others. Both the gateway and its portico had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
units.rightText: and the lodges thereof, and the posts thereof, and the arches thereof, according to these measures: and there were windows therein and in the arches thereof round about; it was fifty cubits long, and five and twenty cubits broad.

units.leftText: Its portico faced the outer court, and its side pillars were decorated with palm trees on each side. Eight steps led up to it.
units.rightText: And the arches thereof were toward the outer court; and palm-trees were upon the posts thereof, on this side, and on that side: and the ascent to it had eight steps.

units.leftText: Then he brought me to the north gate and measured it. It had the same measurements as the others,
units.rightText: And he brought me to the north gate: and he measured it according to these measures;

units.leftText: as did its gate chambers, side pillars, and portico. It also had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
units.rightText: the lodges thereof, the posts thereof, and the arches thereof: and there were windows therein round about; the length was fifty cubits, and the breadth five and twenty cubits.

units.leftText: Its portico faced the outer court, and its side pillars were decorated with palm trees on each side. Eight steps led up to it. Eight Tables for Sacrifices
units.rightText: And the posts thereof were toward the outer court; and palm-trees were upon the posts thereof, on this side, and on that side: and the ascent to it had eight steps.
leftNotes: 40:37 LXX and Vulgate (see also verses 26, 31, and 34); Hebrew jambs or dividing wall

units.leftText: There was a chamber with a doorway by the portico in each of the inner gateways. There the burnt offering was to be washed.
units.rightText: And a chamber with the door thereof was by the posts at the gates; there they washed the burnt-offering.
leftNotes: 40:38 Hebrew at the jambs

units.leftText: Inside the portico of the gateway were two tables on each side, on which the burnt offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings were to be slaughtered.
units.rightText: And in the porch of the gate were two tables on this side, and two tables on that side, to slay thereon the burnt-offering and the sin-offering and the trespass-offering.

units.leftText: Outside, as one goes up to the entrance of the north gateway, there were two tables on one side and two more tables on the other side of the gate’s portico.
units.rightText: And on the one side without, as one goeth up to the entry of the gate toward the north, were two tables; and on the other side, which belonged to the porch of the gate, were two tables.

units.leftText: So there were four tables inside the gateway and four outside — eight tables in all — on which the sacrifices were to be slaughtered.
units.rightText: Four tables were on this side, and four tables on that side, by the side of the gate; eight tables, whereupon they slew the sacrifices.

units.leftText: There were also four tables of dressed stone for the burnt offering, each a cubit and a half long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit high. On these were placed the utensils used to slaughter the burnt offerings and the other sacrifices.
units.rightText: And there were four tables for the burnt-offering, of hewn stone, a cubit and a half long, and a cubit and a half broad, and one cubit high; whereupon they laid the instruments wherewith they slew the burnt-offering and the sacrifice.
leftNotes: 40:42 The tables were approximately 2.6 feet in length and width, and 1.75 feet high (79.2 centimeters in length and width, and 53.3 centimeters high).

units.leftText: The double-pronged hooks, each a handbreadth long, were fastened all around the inside of the room, and the flesh of the offering was to be placed on the tables. Chambers for Ministry
units.rightText: And the hooks, a handbreadth long, were fastened within round about: and upon the tables was the flesh of the oblation.
leftNotes: 40:43 Or shelves
40:43 A handbreadth is approximately 2.9 inches or 7.4 centimeters long.

units.leftText: Outside the inner gate, within the inner court, were two chambers, one beside the north gate and facing south, and another beside the south gate and facing north.
units.rightText: And without the inner gate were chambers for the singers in the inner court, which was at the side of the north gate; and their prospect was toward the south; one at the side of the east gate having the prospect toward the north.
leftNotes: 40:44 LXX; Hebrew within the inner court were chambers for the singers
40:44 LXX; Hebrew the east gateway

units.leftText: Then the man said to me: “The chamber that faces south is for the priests who keep charge of the temple,
units.rightText: And he said unto me, This chamber, whose prospect is toward the south, is for the priests, the keepers of the charge of the house;

units.leftText: and the chamber that faces north is for the priests who keep charge of the altar. These are the sons of Zadok, the only Levites who may approach the LORD to minister before Him.” The Inner Court
units.rightText: and the chamber whose prospect is toward the north is for the priests, the keepers of the charge of the altar: these are the sons of Zadok, who from among the sons of Levi come near to Jehovah to minister unto him.

units.leftText: Next he measured the court. It was square, a hundred cubits long and a hundred cubits wide. And the altar was in front of the temple.
units.rightText: And he measured the court, a hundred cubits long, and a hundred cubits broad, foursquare; and the altar was before the house.

units.leftText: Then he brought me to the portico of the temple and measured the side pillars of the portico to be five cubits on each side. The width of the gateway was fourteen cubits and its sidewalls were three cubits on either side.
units.rightText: Then he brought me to the porch of the house, and measured each post of the porch, five cubits on this side, and five cubits on that side: and the breadth of the gate was three cubits on this side, and three cubits on that side.
leftNotes: 40:48 LXX; the gateway was approximately 24.5 feet or 7.5 meters wide, with sidewalls approximately 5.25 feet or 1.6 meters wide on either side. Hebrew The width of the gateway was three cubits on either side.

units.leftText: The portico was twenty cubits wide and twelve cubits deep, and ten steps led up to it. There were columns by the side pillars, one on each side.
units.rightText: The length of the porch was twenty cubits, and the breadth eleven cubits; even by the steps whereby they went up to it: and there were pillars by the posts, one on this side, and another on that side.
leftNotes: 40:49 20 (long) cubits is approximately 35 feet or 10.7 meters.
40:49 LXX; 12 (long) cubits is approximately 21 feet or 6.4 meters; Hebrew eleven cubits deep; that is, approximately 19.25 feet or 5.9 meters.
40:49 LXX; Hebrew and steps led up to it

units.leftText: Then the man brought me into the outer sanctuary and measured the side pillars to be six cubits wide on each side.
units.rightText: And he brought me to the temple, and measured the posts, six cubits broad on the one side, and six cubits broad on the other side, which was the breadth of the tabernacle.
leftNotes: 41:1 6 (long) cubits is approximately 10.5 feet or 3.2 meters; also in verses 3, 5, and 8.
41:1 One Hebrew manuscript and LXX; most Hebrew manuscripts on each side—the width of the tent

units.leftText: The width of the entrance was ten cubits, and the sides of the entrance were five cubits on each side. He also measured the length of the outer sanctuary to be forty cubits, and the width to be twenty cubits.
units.rightText: And the breadth of the entrance was ten cubits; and the sides of the entrance were five cubits on the one side, and five cubits on the other side: and he measured the length thereof, forty cubits, and the breadth, twenty cubits.
leftNotes: 41:2 10 (long) cubits is approximately 17.5 feet or 5.3 meters.
41:2 5 (long) cubits is approximately 8.75 feet or 2.7 meters; also in verses 9, 11, and 12.
41:2 The outer sanctuary was approximately 70 feet long and 35 feet wide (21.3 meters long and 10.7 meters wide).

units.leftText: And he went into the inner sanctuary and measured the side pillars at the entrance to be two cubits wide. The entrance was six cubits wide, and the walls on each side were seven cubits wide.
units.rightText: Then went he inward, and measured each post of the entrance, two cubits; and the entrance, six cubits; and the breadth of the entrance, seven cubits.
leftNotes: 41:3 2 (long) cubits is approximately 3.5 feet or 1.1 meters.
41:3 7 (long) cubits is approximately 12.25 feet or 3.7 meters.

units.leftText: Then he measured the room adjacent to the inner sanctuary to be twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide. And he said to me, “This is the Most Holy Place. ” Outside the Temple
units.rightText: And he measured the length thereof, twenty cubits, and the breadth, twenty cubits, before the temple: and he said unto me, This is the most holy place.
leftNotes: 41:4 Or the length of the inner sanctuary
41:4 The room was approximately 35 feet long and 35 feet wide (10.7 meters long and 10.7 meters wide).
41:4 Or the Holy of Holies

units.leftText: Next he measured the wall of the temple to be six cubits thick, and the width of each side room around the temple was four cubits.
units.rightText: Then he measured the wall of the house, six cubits; and the breadth of every side-chamber, four cubits, round about the house on every side.
leftNotes: 41:5 4 (long) cubits is approximately 7 feet or 2.1 meters.

units.leftText: The side rooms were arranged one above another in three levels of thirty rooms each. There were ledges all around the wall of the temple to serve as supports for the side rooms, so that the supports would not be fastened into the wall of the temple itself.
units.rightText: And the side-chambers were in three stories, one over another, and thirty in order; and they entered into the wall which belonged to the house for the side-chambers round about, that they might have hold therein, and not have hold in the wall of the house.

units.leftText: The side rooms surrounding the temple widened at each successive level, because the structure surrounding the temple ascended by stages corresponding to the narrowing of the temple wall as it rose upward. And so a stairway went up from the lowest story to the highest, through the middle one.
units.rightText: And the side-chambers were broader as they encompassed the house higher and higher; for the encompassing of the house went higher and higher round about the house: therefore the breadth of the house continued upward; and so one went up from the lowest chamber to the highest by the middle chamber.

units.leftText: I saw that the temple had a raised base all around it, forming the foundation of the side rooms. It was the full length of a rod, six long cubits.
units.rightText: I saw also that the house had a raised basement round about: the foundations of the side-chambers were a full reed of six great cubits.

units.leftText: The outer wall of the side rooms was five cubits thick, and the open area between the side rooms of the temple
units.rightText: The thickness of the wall, which was for the side-chambers, on the outside, was five cubits: and that which was left was the place of the side-chambers that belonged to the house.

units.leftText: and the outer chambers was twenty cubits wide all around the temple.
units.rightText: And between the chambers was a breadth of twenty cubits round about the house on every side.

units.leftText: The side rooms opened into this area, with one entrance on the north and another on the south. The open area was five cubits wide all around.
units.rightText: And the doors of the side-chambers were toward the place that was left, one door toward the north, and another door toward the south: and the breadth of the place that was left was five cubits round about.

units.leftText: Now the building that faced the temple courtyard on the west was seventy cubits wide, and the wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, with a length of ninety cubits.
units.rightText: And the building that was before the separate place at the side toward the west was seventy cubits broad; and the wall of the building was five cubits thick round about, and the length thereof ninety cubits.
leftNotes: 41:12 70 (long) cubits is approximately 122.5 feet or 37.3 meters.
41:12 90 (long) cubits is approximately 157.5 feet or 48 meters.

units.leftText: Then he measured the temple to be a hundred cubits long, and the temple courtyard and the building with its walls were also a hundred cubits long.
units.rightText: So he measured the house, a hundred cubits long; and the separate place, and the building, with the walls thereof, a hundred cubits long;
leftNotes: 41:13 100 (long) cubits is approximately 175 feet or 53.3 meters; similarly in verses 14 and 15.

units.leftText: The width of the temple courtyard on the east, including the front of the temple, was a hundred cubits. The Interior Structures
units.rightText: also the breadth of the face of the house, and of the separate place toward the east, a hundred cubits.

units.leftText: Next he measured the length of the building facing the temple courtyard at the rear of the temple, including its galleries on each side; it was a hundred cubits. The outer sanctuary, the inner sanctuary, and the porticoes facing the court,
units.rightText: And he measured the length of the building before the separate place which was at the back thereof, and the galleries thereof on the one side and on the other side, a hundred cubits; and the inner temple, and the porches of the court;

units.leftText: as well as the thresholds and the beveled windows and the galleries all around with their three levels opposite the threshold, were overlaid with wood on all sides. They were paneled from the ground to the windows, and the windows were covered.
units.rightText: the thresholds, and the closed windows, and the galleries round about on their three stories, over against the threshold, ceiled with wood round about, and from the ground up to the windows (now the windows were covered),

units.leftText: In the space above the outside of the entrance to the inner sanctuary on all the walls, spaced evenly around the inner and outer sanctuary,
units.rightText: to the space above the door, even unto the inner house, and without, and by all the wall round about within and without, by measure.

units.leftText: were alternating carved cherubim and palm trees. Each cherub had two faces:
units.rightText: And it was made with cherubim and palm-trees; and a palm-tree was between cherub and cherub, and every cherub had two faces;

units.leftText: the face of a man was toward the palm tree on one side, and the face of a young lion was toward the palm tree on the other side. They were carved all the way around the temple.
units.rightText: so that there was the face of a man toward the palm-tree on the one side, and the face of a young lion toward the palm-tree on the other side. Thus was it made through all the house round about:

units.leftText: Cherubim and palm trees were carved on the wall of the outer sanctuary from the floor to the space above the entrance.
units.rightText: from the ground unto above the door were cherubim and palm-trees made; thus was the wall of the temple.

units.leftText: The outer sanctuary had a rectangular doorframe, and the doorframe of the sanctuary was similar.
units.rightText: As for the temple, the door-posts were squared; and as for the face of the sanctuary, the appearance thereof was as the appearance of the temple.

units.leftText: There was an altar of wood three cubits high and two cubits square. Its corners, base, and sides were of wood. And the man told me, “This is the table that is before the LORD.”
units.rightText: The altar was of wood, three cubits high, and the length thereof two cubits; and the corners thereof, and the length thereof, and the walls thereof, were of wood: and he said unto me, This is the table that is before Jehovah.
leftNotes: 41:22 Or long; the altar was approximately 5.25 feet high and 3.5 feet square (1.6 meters high and 1.1 meters square)

units.leftText: Both the outer sanctuary and the inner sanctuary had double doors,
units.rightText: And the temple and the sanctuary had two doors.

units.leftText: and each door had two swinging panels. There were two panels for one door and two for the other.
units.rightText: And the doors had two leaves apiece, two turning leaves: two leaves for the one door, and two leaves for the other.

units.leftText: Cherubim and palm trees like those on the walls were carved on the doors of the outer sanctuary, and there was a wooden canopy outside, on the front of the portico.
units.rightText: And there were made on them, on the doors of the temple, cherubim and palm-trees, like as were made upon the walls; and there was a threshold of wood upon the face of the porch without.

units.leftText: There were beveled windows and palm trees on the sidewalls of the portico. The side rooms of the temple also had canopies.
units.rightText: And there were closed windows and palm-trees on the one side and on the other side, on the sides of the porch: thus were the side-chambers of the house, and the thresholds.

units.leftText: Then the man led me out northward into the outer court, and he brought me to the group of chambers opposite the temple courtyard and the outer wall on the north side.
units.rightText: Then he brought me forth into the outer court, the way toward the north: and he brought me into the chamber that was over against the separate place, and which was over against the building toward the north.

units.leftText: The building with the door facing north was a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide.
units.rightText: Before the length of a hundred cubits was the north door, and the breadth was fifty cubits.
leftNotes: 42:2 The building was approximately 175 feet long and 87.5 feet wide (53.3 meters long and 26.7 meters wide).

units.leftText: Gallery faced gallery in three levels opposite the twenty cubits that belonged to the inner court and opposite the pavement that belonged to the outer court.
units.rightText: Over against the twenty cubits which belonged to the inner court, and over against the pavement which belonged to the outer court, was gallery against gallery in the third story.
leftNotes: 42:3 20 (long) cubits is approximately 35 feet or 10.7 meters.

units.leftText: In front of the chambers was an inner walkway ten cubits wide and a hundred cubits long. Their doors were on the north.
units.rightText: And before the chambers was a walk of ten cubits’ breadth inward, a way of one cubit; and their doors were toward the north.
leftNotes: 42:4 LXX. The walkway was approximately 17.5 feet wide and 175 feet long (5.3 meters wide and 53.3 meters long). Hebrew ten cubits wide and a cubit long.

units.leftText: Now the upper chambers were smaller because the galleries took more space from the chambers on the lower and middle floors of the building.
units.rightText: Now the upper chambers were shorter; for the galleries took away from these, more than from the lower and the middlemost, in the building.

units.leftText: For they were arranged in three stories, and unlike the courts, they had no pillars. So the upper chambers were set back further than the lower and middle floors.
units.rightText: For they were in three stories, and they had not pillars as the pillars of the courts: therefore the uppermost was straitened more than the lowest and the middlemost from the ground.

units.leftText: An outer wall in front of the chambers was fifty cubits long and ran parallel to the chambers and the outer court.
units.rightText: And the wall that was without by the side of the chambers, toward the outer court before the chambers, the length thereof was fifty cubits.

units.leftText: For the chambers on the outer court were fifty cubits long, while those facing the temple were a hundred cubits long.
units.rightText: For the length of the chambers that were in the outer court was fifty cubits: and, lo, before the temple were a hundred cubits.

units.leftText: And below these chambers was the entrance on the east side as one enters them from the outer court.
units.rightText: And from under these chambers was the entry on the east side, as one goeth into them from the outer court.

units.leftText: On the south side along the length of the wall of the outer court were chambers adjoining the courtyard and opposite the building,
units.rightText: In the thickness of the wall of the court toward the east, before the separate place, and before the building, there were chambers.
leftNotes: 42:10 LXX; Hebrew east side

units.leftText: with a passageway in front of them, just like the chambers that were on the north. They had the same length and width, with similar exits and dimensions.
units.rightText: And the way before them was like the appearance of the way of the chambers which were toward the north; according to their length so was their breadth: and all their egresses were both according to their fashions, and according to their doors.

units.leftText: And corresponding to the doors of the chambers that were facing south, there was a door in front of the walkway that was parallel to the wall extending eastward.
units.rightText: And according to the doors of the chambers that were toward the south was a door at the head of the way, even the way directly before the wall toward the east, as one entereth into them.

units.leftText: Then the man said to me, “The north and south chambers facing the temple courtyard are the holy chambers where the priests who approach the LORD will eat the most holy offerings. There they will place the most holy offerings— the grain offerings, the sin offerings, and the guilt offerings— for the place is holy.
units.rightText: Then said he unto me, The north chambers and the south chambers, which are before the separate place, they are the holy chambers, where the priests that are near unto Jehovah shall eat the most holy things: there shall they lay the most holy things, and the meal-offering, and the sin-offering, and the trespass-offering; for the place is holy.

units.leftText: Once the priests have entered the holy area, they must not go out into the outer court until they have left behind the garments in which they minister, for these are holy. They are to put on other clothes before they approach the places that are for the people.” The Outer Measurements
units.rightText: When the priests enter in, then shall they not go out of the holy place into the outer court, but there they shall lay their garments wherein they minister; for they are holy: and they shall put on other garments, and shall approach to that which pertaineth to the people.

units.leftText: Now when the man had finished measuring the interior of the temple area, he led me out by the gate that faced east, and he measured the area all around:
units.rightText: Now when he had made an end of measuring the inner house, he brought me forth by the way of the gate whose prospect is toward the east, and measured it round about.

units.leftText: With a measuring rod he measured the east side to be five hundred cubits long.
units.rightText: He measured on the east side with the measuring reed five hundred reeds, with the measuring reed round about.
leftNotes: 42:16 See LXX; five hundred cubits from verse 17 LXX and implied in verses 16, 18, 19, and 20 is approximately 875 feet or 266.7 meters in length. Hebrew five hundred reeds, with the measuring reed round about, that is approximately 5,250 feet or 1,600 meters; similarly in verses 17, 18, 19, and 20.

units.leftText: He measured the north side to be five hundred cubits long.
units.rightText: He measured on the north side five hundred reeds with the measuring reed round about.

units.leftText: He measured the south side to be five hundred cubits long.
units.rightText: He measured on the south side five hundred reeds with the measuring reed.

units.leftText: And he came around and measured the west side to be five hundred cubits long.
units.rightText: He turned about to the west side, and measured five hundred reeds with the measuring reed.

units.leftText: So he measured the area on all four sides. It had a wall all around, five hundred cubits long and five hundred cubits wide, to separate the holy from the common.
units.rightText: He measured it on the four sides: it had a wall round about, the length five hundred, and the breadth five hundred, to make a separation between that which was holy and that which was common.

units.leftText: Then the man brought me back to the gate that faces east,
units.rightText: Afterward he brought me to the gate, even the gate that looketh toward the east.

units.leftText: and I saw the glory of the God of Israel coming from the east. His voice was like the roar of many waters, and the earth shone with His glory.
units.rightText: And, behold, the glory of the God of Israel came from the way of the east: and his voice was like the sound of many waters; and the earth shined with his glory.

units.leftText: The vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when He came to destroy the city and like the visions I had seen by the River Kebar. I fell facedown,
units.rightText: And it was according to the appearance of the vision which I saw, even according to the vision that I saw when I came to destroy the city; and the visions were like the vision that I saw by the river Chebar; and I fell upon my face.
leftNotes: 43:3 Some Hebrew manuscripts and Vulgate; most Hebrew manuscripts when I came

units.leftText: and the glory of the LORD entered the temple through the gate facing east.
units.rightText: And the glory of Jehovah came into the house by the way of the gate whose prospect is toward the east.

units.leftText: Then the Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple.
units.rightText: And the Spirit took me up, and brought me into the inner court; and, behold, the glory of Jehovah filled the house.

units.leftText: While the man was standing beside me, I heard someone speaking to me from inside the temple,
units.rightText: And I heard one speaking unto me out of the house; and a man stood by me.

units.leftText: and He said to me, “Son of man, this is the place of My throne and the place for the soles of My feet, where I will dwell among the Israelites forever. The house of Israel will never again defile My holy name — neither they nor their kings — by their prostitution and by the funeral offerings for their kings at their deaths.
units.rightText: And he said unto me, Son of man, this is the place of my throne, and the place of the soles of my feet, where I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel for ever. And the house of Israel shall no more defile my holy name, neither they, nor their kings, by their whoredom, and by the dead bodies of their kings in their high places;
leftNotes: 43:7 Or the monuments; also in verse 9
43:7 Or for their kings on their high places

units.leftText: When they placed their threshold next to My threshold and their doorposts beside My doorposts, with only a wall between Me and them, they defiled My holy name by the abominations they committed. Therefore I have consumed them in My anger.
units.rightText: in their setting of their threshold by my threshold, and their door-post beside my door-post, and there was but the wall between me and them; and they have defiled my holy name by their abominations which they have committed: wherefore I have consumed them in mine anger.

units.leftText: Now let them remove far from Me their prostitution and the funeral offerings for their kings, and I will dwell among them forever.
units.rightText: Now let them put away their whoredom, and the dead bodies of their kings, far from me; and I will dwell in the midst of them for ever.

units.leftText: As for you, son of man, describe the temple to the people of Israel, so that they may be ashamed of their iniquities. Let them measure the plan,
units.rightText: Thou, son of man, show the house to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities; and let them measure the pattern.

units.leftText: and if they are ashamed of all they have done, then make known to them the design of the temple— its arrangement and its exits and entrances— its whole design along with all its statutes, forms, and laws. Write it down in their sight, so that they may keep its complete design and all its statutes and may carry them out.
units.rightText: And if they be ashamed of all that they have done, make known unto them the form of the house, and the fashion thereof, and the egresses thereof, and the entrances thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the laws thereof; and write it in their sight; that they may keep the whole form thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and do them.
leftNotes: 43:11 Hebrew; LXX and Vulgate and they will be ashamed

units.leftText: This is the law of the temple: All its surrounding territory on top of the mountain will be most holy. Yes, this is the law of the temple. The Altar of Sacrifice
units.rightText: This is the law of the house: upon the top of the mountain the whole limit thereof round about shall be most holy. Behold, this is the law of the house.

units.leftText: These are the measurements of the altar in long cubits (a cubit and a handbreadth): Its gutter shall be a cubit deep and a cubit wide, with a rim of one span around its edge.
units.rightText: And these are the measures of the altar by cubits (the cubit is a cubit and a handbreadth): the bottom shall be a cubit, and the breadth a cubit, and the border thereof by the edge thereof round about a span; and this shall be the base of the altar.
leftNotes: 43:13 The long cubit, about 21 inches or 53.3 centimeters, is the basic unit for linear measurement throughout Ezekiel 40–48.
43:13 One span is approximately 9 inches or 22.9 centimeters.

units.leftText: The space from the gutter on the ground to the lower ledge shall be two cubits, and the ledge one cubit wide. The space from the smaller ledge to the larger ledge shall be four cubits, and the ledge one cubit wide.
units.rightText: And from the bottom upon the ground to the lower ledge shall be two cubits, and the breadth one cubit; and from the lesser ledge to the greater ledge shall be four cubits, and the breadth a cubit.
leftNotes: 43:14 The space was to be approximately 3.5 feet (1.1 meters), and the ledge was to be approximately 1.75 feet wide (53.3 centimeters wide).
43:14 The space was to be approximately 7 feet (2.1 meters), and the ledge was to be approximately 1.75 feet wide (53.3 centimeters wide).

units.leftText: The altar hearth shall be four cubits high, and four horns shall project upward from the hearth.
units.rightText: And the upper altar shall be four cubits; and from the altar hearth and upward there shall be four horns.

units.leftText: The altar hearth shall be square at its four corners, twelve cubits long and twelve cubits wide.
units.rightText: And the altar hearth shall be twelve cubits long by twelve broad, square in the four sides thereof.
leftNotes: 43:16 12 (long) cubits is approximately 21 feet or 6.4 meters.

units.leftText: The ledge shall also be square, fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits wide, with a rim of half a cubit and a gutter of a cubit all around it. The steps of the altar shall face east.”
units.rightText: And the ledge shall be fourteen cubits long by fourteen broad in the four sides thereof; and the border about it shall be half a cubit; and the bottom thereof shall be a cubit round about; and the steps thereof shall look toward the east.
leftNotes: 43:17 14 (long) cubits is approximately 24.5 feet or 7.5 meters.
43:17 A half cubit is approximately 10.5 inches or 26.7 centimeters.

units.leftText: Then He said to me: “Son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘These are the statutes for the altar on the day it is constructed, so that burnt offerings may be sacrificed on it and blood may be splattered on it:
units.rightText: And he said unto me, Son of man, thus saith the Lord Jehovah: These are the ordinances of the altar in the day when they shall make it, to offer burnt-offerings thereon, and to sprinkle blood thereon.

units.leftText: You are to give a young bull from the herd as a sin offering to the Levitical priests who are of the family of Zadok, who approach Me to minister before Me, declares the Lord GOD.
units.rightText: Thou shalt give to the priests the Levites that are of the seed of Zadok, who are near unto me, to minister unto me, saith the Lord Jehovah, a young bullock for a sin-offering.

units.leftText: You are to take some of its blood and put it on the four horns of the altar, on the four corners of the ledge, and all around the rim; thus you will cleanse the altar and make atonement for it.
units.rightText: And thou shalt take of the blood thereof, and put it on the four horns of it, and on the four corners of the ledge, and upon the border round about: thus shalt thou cleanse it and make atonement for it.

units.leftText: Then you are to take away the bull for the sin offering and burn it in the appointed part of the temple area outside the sanctuary.
units.rightText: Thou shalt also take the bullock of the sin-offering, and it shall be burnt in the appointed place of the house, without the sanctuary.

units.leftText: On the second day you are to present an unblemished male goat as a sin offering, and the altar is to be cleansed as it was with the bull.
units.rightText: And on the second day thou shalt offer a he-goat without blemish for a sin-offering; and they shall cleanse the altar, as they did cleanse it with the bullock.

units.leftText: When you have finished the purification, you are to present a young, unblemished bull and an unblemished ram from the flock.
units.rightText: When thou hast made an end of cleansing it, thou shalt offer a young bullock without blemish, and a ram out of the flock without blemish.

units.leftText: You must present them before the LORD; the priests are to sprinkle salt on them and sacrifice them as a burnt offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: And thou shalt bring them near before Jehovah, and the priests shall cast salt upon them, and they shall offer them up for a burnt-offering unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: For seven days you are to provide a male goat daily for a sin offering; you are also to provide a young bull and a ram from the flock, both unblemished.
units.rightText: Seven days shalt thou prepare every day a goat for a sin-offering: they shall also prepare a young bullock, and a ram out of the flock, without blemish.

units.leftText: For seven days the priests are to make atonement for the altar and cleanse it; so they shall consecrate it.
units.rightText: Seven days shall they make atonement for the altar and purify it; so shall they consecrate it.
leftNotes: 43:26 Hebrew fill its hand
